reuse.why: Builds on the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend, getNextDate and getNextDateAfter; schedule-template now walks occurrences with getNextDate/getNextDateAfter instead of its own weekend loop, and the new range handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule.

duplication.why: Removes the twice-written weekend ternary from schedule-template, but the `skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(...) : date` decision is still written twice: as resolveDate inside getNextDate and as a local applyWeekendRule in schedules/app.ts.

placement.why: The weekend/holiday rule, its search-window bounds and the holiday matcher live in shared/schedules.ts; the enable-flag wrapper is placed privately in server/schedules/app.ts rather than beside the rule it wraps.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps (daily skip, range handler, holidays, yearly holidays) plus tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: One function decides moving, skipping (null for daily) and holiday matching, so later rule changes land once; the heuristic search windows (7 or 2 days times 1 + number of holidays) are opaque bounds callers must remember to apply.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every weekend adjustment (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, schedule-template via getNextDate) goes through getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: The enable-flag wrapper exists twice under different names: `resolveDate` in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate and `applyWeekendRule` in server/schedules/app.ts, both `skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(date, mode, frequency, holidays) : date`.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains frequency and holidays parameters and a `frequency === 'daily'` branch returning null; these encode the requested rules, and all callers route through it, though the enable-flag check stays at two wrapper sites.
